text:
Tanya: FYI a Private customer is seeing websocket streaming responses go silent ~25-35s into the stream. They say the socket stays ESTABLISHED but no chunks for a while, then data resumes. Happening only from their VPC.
Ben: Got it. Do we have repro steps / sample request? Which model & region? Any TLS errors in our gateway logs?
Tanya: Repro steps from customer (anonymized):
```
# reproduce with wscat
wscat -c \"wss://private-gw.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-mini\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\"
# they send a prompt and then observe silence after ~30s
```
They attached a short pcap snippet and this tcpdump tail: 
```
IP 10.1.2.3.54321 > 10.2.3.4.443: Flags [P.], seq 123:456, ack 98, win 217, length 333
IP 10.2.3.4.443 > 10.1.2.3.54321: Flags [.], ack 456, win 501, length 0
# repeated zero-length payloads, then long silence, then payload resumes
```
They also saw in their proxy logs a TLS renegotiation triggered by a middlebox: `TLS handshake: renegotiation` and an HTTP CONNECT logged as `200 Connection Established` but then the appliance buffered and released bytes only after an idle timer.
Ben: Sounds like an intermediate device (customer firewall / DPI proxy) is doing buffering / idle-close behavior. Common culprits: stateful firewalls that aggregate small chunks, deep packet inspection that waits for application-level termination, or TCP keepalive/idle timeout on the path.
Ryan: Can we confirm from our side: any SNI or ALPN mismatches? If the appliance rewraps TLS / terminates TLS, it can break our streaming semantics. Tanya, did they use SNI-preserving egress?
Tanya: Customer says egress goes through a corporate proxy appliance that performs SSL inspection. They also have an egress allowlist by hostname, not IP, and their DNS TTL is low/fast-failover.
Ben: Steps I'd run/check: 
- ask customer for a packet capture around the silent period (pcap). Look for RSTs, window shrink, duplicated ACKs, or re-initiated TLS handshakes.
- check our gateway logs for the connection id / client_ip and whether we saw a FIN/RST or application-level close.
- confirm ALPN (http/1.1 vs h2) and SNI. If the proxy rewraps TLS and changes ALPN, buffering may occur.
- try forcing websocket pings (application-level) every 10s to keep middlebox from idling.
- repro from an instance in their VPC if they can share a small bastion.
Ryan: Add network suggestions we gave to other customers: 
1) Ensure egress allowlist includes our edge IP ranges (we provided `35.198.0.0/16` etc in onboarding).
2) If they have SSL inspection, configure it to treat `wss` endpoints as passthrough or to allow full-duplex streaming (some appliances have a \"websocket passthrough\" toggle).
3) Increase TCP idle timeout on the appliance to >120s or enable TCP keepalives.
Tanya: I ran a quick grep on the pcap they sent — I see a TLS ClientHello, then `Server Hello`, then ~30s later a new `Client Hello` (reneg). That lines up with the silent window.
Ben: Two hypotheses: 
A) Middlebox is re-negotiating SSL and buffering frames until it completes inspection.
B) Middlebox has an application-level idle flush policy that \"chunks\" small writes and only forwards them on timer or size threshold (corking).
Ben: Quick repro command we asked them to run to isolate DNS/eDNS behavior:
```
# simple curl websocket probe (non-WS, but shows egress path)
curl -vI https://private-gw.redwood.example/health --resolve private-gw.redwood.example:443:203.0.113.12
```
Tanya: Customer tried toggling with & without corporate proxy and reported the issue disappears when bypassing the appliance (direct internet). So it's definitely their middlebox. They've now done two concrete things: added websocket passthrough rule (no TLS inspect) and enabled keepalives — both reduced incidents.
Ryan: Can we document a recommended checklist for support/SE to send next time? I'll draft but first: include examples of logs we look for on our side and minimal commands to suggest to customers (wscat, tcpdump filter, curl --resolve).
InfraBot: Note added to support playbook: `ws-silence-middlebox` with suggested steps: check ALPN/SNI, confirm egress allowlist by IP, request pcap, recommend websocket keepalive 10s, suggest firewall passthrough or idle timeout >120s.
Tanya: Customer confirmed final fix: disabling deep packet inspection for our host + adding keepalive. They saw steady streaming for 1 hour with no pauses. 
Ben: Great. Closing notes: mark case with root cause = "customer middlebox TLS inspection and aggressive idle/chunking behavior"; recommend we include network guidance in Private onboarding docs.
Tanya: I'll update the support ticket and onboarding doc. :thumbsup:
